thread:
jordan: quick opinion check 1 Create Policy form. two parts: 1) when to show inline validation vs a top summary, 2) how to mark required fields (asterisk, 'Required' tag, or both). also debate on confirmation for 'Remove all policies' 1 typed confirm vs simple checkbox.

 sophia: my take: immediate inline validation is great for fields with single, deterministic rules (email, name). if a field has multiple possible errors (format, reserved word, backend conflict) show inline but also show a compact summary on submit that links to each field.

 liam: agree. for very short forms (2-3 fields) inline-only is fine. for multi-step or long forms, users appreciate a short summary so they don't have to hunt. we should also show error counts per section.

 jordan: what about required markers? ive seen confusion when asterisks are used without legend. users expect an explicit 'Required' label especially when we also show optional markers.

 maya (a11y): accessibility rules: never rely on color or asterisk alone. use aria-required on inputs and include visible text for screen-reader-only or visually present "Required". if we use an asterisk, add aria-hidden="true" on it and provide descriptive text with aria-label or visually-hidden span. error announcements: use aria-live="assertive" for submit-time errors, polite for inline suggestions. focus management: when submit fails, focus to the summary container then offer keyboard link to first invalid field.

 sophia: love that. small copy ask: rather than 'Required' maybe use 'Required field' or 'Required' short enough? i'm fine with 'Required' as label, just be consistent.

 liam: bulk delete: typed confirm is safest but sometimes overkill. suggest threshold: if user selects more than 10 items or "Remove all" -> typed confirm. otherwise checkbox + destructive CTA is ok. include count and list first 3 items.

 jordan: agree on threshold. copy examples: 
- modal title: "Confirm remove policies"
- body: "This will permanently remove 12 policies from Workspace X. This action cannot be undone."
- typed variant: "Type REMOVE to confirm"

 maya (a11y): ensure typed input has aria-describedby that explains exact text to type and that errors are announced. also trap focus inside modal and ensure keyboard-only users can cancel with Esc. if using typed confirm, allow pasting? i'd recommend disabling paste to force conscious typing. note: disabling paste has pros/cons for accessibility; if disabling, make it clear.

 sophia: good call on paste. i'm leaning to allow paste for people using password managers or macros, but show a small tooltip: "Typing is recommended to prevent accidental confirmation."

 liam: technical note: backend should accept either case-insensitive match and trim whitespace. show inline validation: 'value doesn't match' with hint.

 design-bot: uploaded: Figma frame "policy-form-validation_v1" :paperclip: (link)

 jordan: action items: 1) add two validation modes in the spec: inline-live for compact forms, hybrid (inline + summary on submit) for long/multi-section forms; 2) required marker: use explicit 'Required' label with optional asterisk as visual shorthand; programmatically set aria-required; 3) destructive flow: checkbox for small selections, typed confirm for >10 or "Remove all" with count and irreversible copy; 4) a11y: aria-live rules, focus to summary, focus trap in modal, consider paste policy for typed confirm and document accessibility tradeoffs. i'll update the figma and create a small PR for copy. ping @sophia @maya for review. :wave:
